messages:
joe_acme: Hey team — since ~2026-03-15 20:12 UTC our integration started getting lots of 504/503 for streaming generate calls. SDK is hitting retry loops and customers see long waits. Example request-id: req_20260315_9f3b. Can share logs if helpful

lina_cs: Sorry you're seeing this, Joe. Can you paste a sample request (no PII) and the SDK version? Also are these blocking all traffic or a subset?

joe_acme: Using Redwood JS SDK v2.4.1, streaming chat generate, long system prompts (10-15k tokens). Example minimal repro (redacted):
```js
const res = await client.chat.stream({
  model: 'openredwood-large',
  messages: [{role:'system',content:'<redacted long prompt>'}, {role:'user',content:'hello'}],
  stream: true
});
```
Errors: sometimes 503 then client retries and gets 504. Request id header returned sometimes: req_20260315_9f3b

alex_support: Thanks — we're on it. Repro steps we'll try: 1) run same request via curl to isolate SDK vs network; 2) check edge/gateway logs with request-id; 3) try shorter prompt to see token-length correlation. For now we'll set sticky-route to bypass the problematic edge if possible.

sanjay_oncall: I grabbed the request-id from our logs. We're seeing a spike in edge upstream timeouts around that window; proxy reports backend connections exhausted for the tenant pool. Stack excerpt: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T20:12:17Z WARN upstream_timeout req=req_20260315_9f3b backend=hosted-infer-01 conn_wait=1.2s queue=85
[poolmgr] 2026-03-15T20:12:17Z ERROR conn_pool_exhausted tenant=acme-integ active=102 limit=100
```
Looks like connection pool for that tenant momentarily hit limit and we returned 504/503.

maya_sre: We're seeing correlated TCP FINs from an egress NAT node causing ephemeral conn churn; pool manager didn't age conns fast enough. Short-term mitigation: bump per-tenant pool cap and reduce connection keepalive window to recycle stale sockets. Will apply a canary change to one edge.

opsbot: Deploy started: change=pool-cap-bump+keepalive-shorten canary=edge-usw2-1 by maya_sre at 2026-03-15T20:30Z

alex_support: Joe, while we rollout a canary we recommend turning on SDK non-streaming fallback (stream:false) for critical paths or reduce prompt length to <8k tokens as a temporary workaround. Also add client-level exponential backoff with jitter to avoid thundering:
```js
await retry(async () => client.chat.create(...), {retries:5, minTimeout:200, maxTimeout:2000, jitter:true});
```

joe_acme: Thanks — can try fallback. Any ETA on fix? Customers are seeing intermittent failures right now.

opsbot: Canary deploy succeeded on edge-usw2-1 at 2026-03-15T20:33:02Z; health=ok; error-rate reduced 80% on that segment.

sanjay_oncall: Canary looks good. Rolling change to remaining edges with staged ramp. We'll monitor p95 and 5xx.

maya_sre: Rollout started to other edges at 20:40Z. Monitoring queue depth and conn stats.

alex_support: Update for Joe — we've rolled out mitigations. Please try the same request and let us know if you still see 5xx/504. If you can still reproduce, please grab the request-id and timestamp and we'll pull full packet-level logs.

joe_acme: Re-tested at 20:52Z: one 504 for req_20260315_b12c, then everything else OK. Will send logs and enable fallback for critical flows. Thanks for fast response :thumbsup: :eyes:

lina_cs: We'll follow up with a short postmortem and guidance on SDK retries/stream fallbacks and recommended pool settings for large prompt workloads.

opsbot: Incident ticket updated: INC-2026-0315-edgesock. Severity: P2. Owner: maya_sre.

alex_support: Closing loop here — long-term fixes: improve pool eviction heuristics, add per-tenant adaptive caps, and instrument prompt-length routing to avoid large-token streams on small pools. We'll notify your account once change is in prod.

joe_acme: Appreciate it. Please cc our security contact on postmortem.
